Usage: glimmervoid [command] [options]

With no command, starts the server.

Commands:
  doctor              Check the install, PATH, agent CLIs and native module, then exit
  settings <cmd>      Read and change config.json: list, get, describe, set, unset, search, schema (each takes --json)
  host <cmd>          Register machines this dashboard links over ssh: add, list, remove
  packs <cmd>         Build a pack: guide, check <folder>, preview <folder>, list
  pr-flows check      Check PR flows sources, actions and rules; --pr <url> runs each approved source once
  pr-action report    Report a PR action run's outcome from the command it ran (--outcome, --message)
  github-usage        Show the GitHub calls and rate-limit points Glimmervoid spent in the last hour beside the account pool (--json)
  pair                Mint a single-use pairing link for a remote device
  pair --list         List paired devices
  pair --revoke <id>  Revoke a paired device
  agent setup grok    Install the Grok hook relay, which does nothing outside Glimmervoid
  vault               Run the vault companion that reads approved secrets from 1Password; --server <url> serves another machine
  doorman             Run the doorman, which forwards each tenant's traffic, wakes its server and hosts its watcher

Inside a Glimmervoid session:
  spawn <prompt>      Start a session on that prompt, with its own dashboard card, that this session owns until its task is done. An option beside an in-process subagent when the work should run in its own supervised session and worktree
  send [child] <text> Message a session this one spawned; a spawned session messages its parent with send <text>. Use it to steer a spawned session, or to report back to the parent
  read [child]        Read what this session's spawned sessions sent; a spawned session reads its parent's messages. Use it when a spawned session or the parent has messaged this session
  close <child>       End a session this one spawned and discard its worktree; refused while it holds unpushed work unless --discard. Use it once a spawned session's work has landed or is no longer wanted
  answer <child> <json>|--operator Answer a spawned session's held question, or pass it to the operator with --operator. Use it when a spawned session waits on a question this session can settle
  attention <note>    Flag this session as needing the operator. Use it when the task is blocked on the operator, such as a refused call a retry will not change
  sessions            List the live sessions. Use it to see what other sessions are working on before touching shared code
  push                Land this session's commits on the integration branch and push it. Use it when this session's commits are ready to land
  edit <path>         Open a text file for the operator to edit in the dashboard. Use it when the operator should write or correct text, such as a plan or a prompt
  review <pr>         Queue a team review of a pull request; the draft waits in the Reviews tab for the operator to post. Use it instead of gh pr review when a pull request needs a review the operator posts
  reviews [pr]        List the Reviews tab: reviews running, queued and drafted; with a pull request, read its draft in full. Use it to follow a queued review or read its draft
  prs                 List the operator's open pull requests with their checks, reviews and merge state. Use it to find which of the operator's pull requests need work
  link-pr <pr>        Link a pull request to this session's card. Use it after opening a pull request for this session's work
  packs guide|check|list Read how to build a pack (its schema, the panel bridge and example packs to copy), check a pack folder, or list the packs installed here. Use it before writing or changing a Glimmervoid pack, and to check one before asking the operator to approve it
  settings list|get   Read Glimmervoid's settings; a secret shows only as configured or not. Use it instead of reading config.json
  why <file>:<line>   Name the session, agent, task and prompt that made the commit owning a line (or pass a commit sha). Use it before changing code another session wrote, to learn what that session was asked
  whiteboard new|list|connect|disconnect|get|put|render|delete|plan Create, connect to, read, edit, plan on and delete a shared whiteboard the operator and connected sessions edit together. Use it to plan or explain a design with the operator or other sessions
  checkout <repo>     Make a worktree of a configured project or a local git repository, owned by this session and removed when it closes. Use it instead of git worktree add or git clone when this session must change a repository it was not started in
  need <NAME>...      Ask for secrets by environment variable name; once the operator approves, Glimmervoid writes them to .env.local in this session's directory and never shows the values; exits 0 delivered, 10 pending, 20 denied, 30 companion offline, 1 failed. Use it when the task needs an API key or other secret, instead of asking the operator to paste it into chat
  arena start|races|race|judge|diff Start an Arena race, list races, read one race, start judging it, or read one contestant's diff (arena start <spec json>, arena race <race>, arena judge <race>, arena diff <race> <contestant>). Use it to race one prompt across agent setups in this session's project, follow a race, judge it, or read a contestant's diff
  comments list|reply|resolve List the open review comments the operator left on this session's changes, reply to one (comments reply <id> <text>), or resolve one (comments resolve <id>). Use it when the operator leaves a review comment on your changes, to answer it and close it
  wake in|at|cron|list|cancel Have Glimmervoid type a prompt into this session later, once it is idle and the operator is not typing (wake in 15m <text>, wake at 14:30 <text>, wake cron "0 9 * * 1-5" <text>, wake list, wake cancel <id>); times use the operator's timezone. Use it to come back to a task later, such as checking a rollout or a slow job, instead of polling or sleeping
  limits              List which of these commands answer here and why the rest do not. Use it when a command is refused, to see why
  ssh-sign            Sign a commit with the operator's forwarded ssh agent (git runs this)

Options:
  --port <number>     Server port (default: 3000)
  --config <path>     Config file (default: ~/.glimmervoid/config.json)
  --name <label>      Name for the device being paired (with pair)
  --no-open           Do not open the dashboard in a browser on first start
  --version           Print the version
  --help, -h          Print this help
